claims.statement: Jekyll overview covers FPT/GHEC/GHES; included recommendation favors Actions deployment while body recommends Jekyll as generator. Generator choice and deployment mechanism are separate; neither recommendation is accepted estate policy.

Jekyll transforms Markdown/HTML with layouts and Liquid into static output. Source says Windows is not officially supported and links workarounds; links are not executed installations or current runtime assurance.

Most settings use _config.yml, but Pages-managed configuration fixes lsi false, safe true, source top level, incremental false, Rouge highlighter, gist noscript false and kramdown MathJax/Rouge. Scope is managed Jekyll build, not proof arbitrary custom/local workflow settings are immutable.

Default exclusions cover node_modules/vendor, underscore/dot/hash-leading names, tilde suffix and configured exclude; include can request processing. Default exclusion is not a universal privacy guarantee because explicit includes and custom build behavior can expose files.
YAML front matter supplies page/post title, layout and metadata; site.github can expose repository metadata. Presence does not verify rendered metadata correctness or safe publication.

Themes can customize presentation and override defaults; cloud supports listed themes and manual other open-source themes, GHES wording emphasizes manual addition. Open-source label or link is not per-file distribution clearance.

Managed Pages default plugins listed as non-disableable include coffeescript, default-layout, gist, github-metadata, optional-front-matter, paginate, readme-index, titles-from-headings and relative-links. This historical list is not a live dependency/version inventory.

Additional supported plugin gems can be declared in _config.yml plugins; unsupported plugins cannot be built by managed Pages, so local generation and static-output publishing are offered. Custom/local code still requires review; no upstream plugin executed.

Source suggests updating github-pages gem for plugin versions and links hosted versions JSON; freshness suggestion does not prove immutable dependencies, compatibility, current version resolution or authorized upgrades.

Rouge is default and Pygments configuration falls back to Rouge; another configured Jekyll highlighter yields warning. Lowercase fenced language identifiers are required per source; runtime rendering not tested.

Alternative client-side highlighting requires disabling Jekyll highlighting through kramdown syntax_highlighter_opts disable. rougify style example writes style.css and could overwrite content; it was not executed or accepted as safe default.

Local preview precedes publication where desired. Branch changes merged into source and custom workflow triggers describe publication intent subject to trigger exclusions and successful deployment; local test or workflow file is not native behavior evidence.
